## Summary
Reviewed head 4eaff18b. The mapped-IPv6 branch of `isLoopbackHost` now calls the existing `mappedV6ToV4` (ssrf-guard.js) and is loopback only if the embedded IPv4 starts with `127.`. All three acceptance criteria are met and tested. No Critical findings.

## Strengths
- Reuses the one existing mapped-address parser instead of adding a third predicate (DRY). `ssrf-guard.js` imports only `node:net`, so there is no cycle and no new weight.
- Tests go red against the old prefix match (I reverted the fix in place: 2 of 18 tests fail, restored afterwards) and cover both the criterion cases and the boundaries (7e00, 8000, extra hextets, malformed dotted tails).
- Callers verified: bind-host.test, connection-locality.test, host-mdns-integration.test, ws-exposure.test, ssrf-guard.test, github-webhook.test, server-cli-banner.test and lan-ip.test all pass (127.x, ::1, localhost, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, uppercase true; 0.0.0.0 and private ranges false).
- Widening check: a 200k-input differential fuzz of valid IPv6 literals (normalised via URL) against "::1 or mapped with first byte 127" found zero inputs newly classified loopback that are not. `::ffff:0:7f00:1`, `::127.0.0.1` (IPv4-compatible), `64:ff9b::7f00:1`, `%lo0` zone ids and bracketed hosts all return false.

## Critical
None.

## Suggestions
- The expanded form `0:0:0:0:0:ffff:7f00:1` (and `0::ffff:...`) is now loopback via the full parse. It is genuinely 127.0.0.1, so this is correct. It goes beyond the criterion's letter ("first mapped hextet is four hex digits 7f00-7fff"), but within its intent: `::ffff:7f00:0001` also qualifies, as the criterion allows. Optionally pin one expanded-form case in the tests so the behaviour is deliberate (cheap, fold).
- The commit message lacks a `Trial-Closes:` line; the PR body has it. Add the trailer to the commit if the rule applies per commit (cheap, fold).

## Nitpicks
- `::ffff:127.0.0.1%lo0` was previously true (prefix) and is now false. This is correct narrowing and no caller depends on it; no change needed.
- Non-mapped `::1` spellings (`::0001`, `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1`) are still not loopback. This predates the PR and is out of scope.

## Verdict
Approve
